- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overestimation, apply a 10–15% downward correction in the next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to the next forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and forecast diverges from true outcome by >3%, use mean reversion: align forecast to 20-day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimistic tail-end forecasts; cap final 3–5 days at 10% below peak if sentiment is weak or neutral.
